title: Concavity of a squared profile difference
statement: Let $a,b\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $b\ge0$, $a-b>0$, $a+b<1$, and $a\le\tfrac12$. If $U$ is the Gaussian isoperimetric profile defined by applying the standard Gaussian density to the lower Gaussian quantile, then $x\mapsto U(a+x)^2-U(a-x)^2$ is concave on $[0,b]$.
replaced: Let $\Phi$ and $\varphi$ be the standard Gaussian distribution function and density, and put $Q=\Phi^{-1}$ and $I(p)=\varphi(Q(p))$ for $0<p<1$. If $b\ge0$, $a-b>0$, $a+b<1$, and $a\le1/2$, then $x\mapsto I(a+x)^2-I(a-x)^2$ is concave on $[0,b]$.
